page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.24xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server built on 64-bit ARMv9 architecture featuring 96 physical cores powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 192.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated physical core. Hardware storage features a bundled 5700 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, while networking is backed by 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluation highlights exceptional multi-threaded performance. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core execution, PassMark physics testing, and Geekbench software compilation with Clang. Memory subsystem throughput is high, reaching 480.66 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The combined storage and processing capacity yields 195.84 million operations/sec in Redis SET benchmarks, 102.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and top-tier PassMark database operation scores, while single-core performance metrics remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, integrating 5700 GB of fast local NVMe SSD directly with 96 cores provides strong cost efficiency for high-IOPS applications without requiring external block storage allocation. Key tradeoffs include modest single-core execution speed and the absence of discrete GPU hardware, which limits peak performance for accelerated graphics or pure GPU deep learning tasks.

The server is well suited for memory-bound parallel processing, high-concurrency database deployments, large software build pipelines, static web serving clusters, and CPU-bound LLM text generation tasks using medium to large models.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.24xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM-based instance powered by 96 physical cores of AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio, alongside 5700 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and outstanding database and Redis SET operations throughput. The integrated local NVMe SSD offers strong cost efficiency for storage-heavy compute workloads by reducing reliance on external remote storage volumes. Primary tradeoffs include average single-threaded CPU speed and the lack of dedicated GPU accelerators. The c8gd.24xlarge is optimal for high-concurrency database systems, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, and multi-core data processing jobs.
